# Spatial India

> Standardised district-level data for India. Indicators from Indian government sources — Census 2011, NFHS-5, NCRB, RBI, the Agricultural Census, MSME and others — joined onto one district geography, so they can be mapped, ranked and compared against each other. Free for personal and non-commercial use, with attribution.

Districts are addressed by `objectid`, not by name: four district names each belong to two states. Resolve a name with `GET /v1/districts?q=<name>`, which returns every match with its state.

Values are `null` where a source never covered that district — never zero. Each value carries its own `estimated` flag, per district rather than per source. Every API response includes the source, vintage and caveat of each indicator; quote those alongside the number.

## API

- [REST API](https://api.spatialindia.com/v1/indicators): free, keyless, read-only. Four endpoints — `/v1/indicators`, `/v1/districts`, `/v1/districts/{objectid}`, `/v1/boundaries/{objectid}.geojson`
- [OpenAPI document](https://api.spatialindia.com/v1/openapi.json): the full schema for every endpoint and response
- [MCP server](https://api.spatialindia.com/mcp): streamable HTTP, no auth. Six tools — find_indicator, get_district, compare_districts, rank_districts, get_methodology, build_map_link
- [API documentation](https://spatialindia.com/api-platform): endpoints, MCP install snippets and examples
- [The same documentation as Markdown](https://spatialindia.com/api-platform.md): install steps for every client, the tool list, worked examples with real numbers, limits and caveats — one file, generated from the same corpus the API serves

## Site

- [Map](https://spatialindia.com/app): the interactive map. Deep-linkable — `?layers=<dataset_id>` draws one indicator, `?biv=<id>,<id>` draws two, `?state=<State>` zooms, `?district=<objectid>` opens a district profile, `?studio=1` opens Map Studio on that view
- [Map Studio](https://spatialindia.com/map-studio): publication-ready map images (SVG, PNG, PDF) with source credit and Survey of India boundaries, made in the browser
- [Datasets](https://spatialindia.com/datasets): every dataset with its source, vintage and coverage
- [Methodology](https://spatialindia.com/methodology): how sources are harmonised onto one district geography
- [Caveats](https://spatialindia.com/caveats): what each layer does not say, per source
- [States](https://spatialindia.com/states): per-state profiles
- [Stories](https://spatialindia.com/stories): worked analyses using the data

## Using this data

- [How to cite](https://spatialindia.com/cite): citation string and the per-source attribution each licence requires
- [Embed](https://spatialindia.com/embed): an embeddable map widget for articles and reports
- [Terms](https://spatialindia.com/terms)

Spatial India is not a government body and the data is not official. It is a harmonisation of published government releases; where a figure matters, check it against the source named in the response.

# Spatial India — district data for AI agents and applications

India's public district data, cleaned and crosswalked onto one geography: 134 indicators across 800+ districts, 14 domains, 10+ official sources. Free, keyless and read-only, over an MCP server and a REST API.

- MCP server: `https://api.spatialindia.com/mcp` (streamable HTTP, POST only, no authentication)
- REST base: `https://api.spatialindia.com/v1`
- OpenAPI: `https://api.spatialindia.com/v1/openapi.json`
- Dataset version: 2026-09-20
- Docs: https://spatialindia.com/api-platform

## MCP tools

| Tool | Arguments | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `find_indicator` | `query` | Say “stunting” or “land inequality” — it returns the exact indicator, its unit and its source. |
| `get_district` | `name`, `state?`, `indicators?` | Two districts are named Bilaspur. It hands back both and asks which — it never quietly picks one. |
| `compare_districts` | `districts[]`, `indicators[]` | Jaipur, Indore and Patna on health, literacy and credit — columns never published together, in one call. |
| `rank_districts` | `indicator`, `scope?`, `order?`, `limit?` | Best or worst, nationwide or inside one state. Districts a survey missed never fake an extreme. |
| `get_methodology` | `indicator?` | Source, year, definition, caveat and a citation you can paste — before the figure reaches print. |
| `build_map_link` | `indicators[]`, `state?`, `districts?`, `view?` | Every answer links a live map — ready to explore interactively, screenshot, or embed. |

## Worked examples

### Which districts in Uttar Pradesh have the worst child stunting?

1. `find_indicator({ query: "child stunting" })` — Resolved to nfhs5_stunting. Ids are not guessable, so this comes first.
1. `rank_districts({ indicator: "nfhs5_stunting", scope: "Uttar Pradesh", order: "desc", limit: 3 })` — 75 of 75 districts in scope carry a value. Uncovered ones sort last, never as an extreme.
1. `get_methodology({ indicator: "nfhs5_stunting" })` — The definition, the vintage and the attribution — before the number is stated.

The three worst-affected districts in Uttar Pradesh, out of the 75 the survey reached:

|   | District | Child Stunting |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bahraich | 52.1% |
| 2 | Budaun | 51.8% |
| 3 | Sambhal | 51.6% |

Height-for-age below −2 SD (WHO Child Growth Standard). National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 2019–21. Every district in the state is covered.

Map: https://spatialindia.com/app?state=Uttar+Pradesh&layers=nfhs5_stunting

### Tell me about Bilaspur.

1. `get_district({ name: "Bilaspur" })` — Two districts share the name. The tool returns both rather than choosing one.

There are two. Which one do you mean?

| District | State | objectid | Population 2011 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bilaspur | Himachal Pradesh | 62 | 3,81,956 |
| Bilaspur | Chhattisgarh | 134 | 16,25,502 |

Bilaspur, Balrampur, Hamirpur and Pratapgarh each name two districts in different states. Every district is addressed by objectid rather than by name, which is what lets the tool hand back both instead of answering confidently about the wrong place.

### Compare Jaipur, Indore and Patna on literacy, child stunting and bank credit.

1. `find_indicator({ query: "literacy stunting bank credit" })` — Three ids, from three different sources and three different years.
1. `compare_districts({ districts: ["Jaipur","Indore","Patna"], indicators: ["census2011_literacy_rate","nfhs5_stunting","rbi_credit_per_capita"] })` — One call across three domains, not three lookups.

Three districts, three domains, one row each:

| District | Literacy Rate — Total | Child Stunting | Bank Credit Per Capita |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jaipur, Rajasthan | 75.5% | 25.0% | ₹45,565 |
| Indore, Madhya Pradesh | 80.9% | 28.7% | ₹35,783 |
| Patna, Bihar | 70.7% | 34.5% | ₹15,450 |

Three vintages on one row — literacy 2011, stunting 2019–21, credit 2026. Every response carries the source and vintage of each column, so the comparison can be stated honestly rather than silently averaged across a decade.

Map: https://spatialindia.com/app?biv=census2011_literacy_rate%2Crbi_credit_per_capita&pal=greenblue

## REST endpoints

### `GET /v1/indicators` — The catalogue

Every indicator id with its unit, source, vintage, caveat, estimation method, ranking polarity, district coverage and how many of those districts report a hard zero. Start here — ids are stable and are what every other endpoint takes.

| Parameter | Type | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `q` | string | Free-text filter. Every word must appear in the id, name, description, category, source or caveat. |
| `limit` | integer | Page size. |
| `offset` | integer | Page offset. |

Example: `https://api.spatialindia.com/v1/indicators?q=land+inequality`

### `GET /v1/districts` — The table

Without `indicators` this is the district directory. With them it is the joined table, sorted and paged. Ranking, comparison and name search are all this one endpoint.

| Parameter | Type | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | string | Restrict to one state. |
| `q` | string | District name or a known alternative spelling. Exact match first, substring only if nothing matched exactly. Returns every match with its state. |
| `indicators` | csv | Up to 5 indicator ids. |
| `sort` | string | A field: objectid, district, state, population_2011, area_sqkm, or an indicator you asked for. This names a field — direction is `order`. |
| `order` | asc \| desc | Defaults to asc. |
| `limit` | integer | Max 100, defaults to 50. |
| `offset` | integer | Page offset. |

Example: `https://api.spatialindia.com/v1/districts?q=bilaspur`

### `GET /v1/districts/{objectid}` — One district in full

Every published indicator for one district in a single call. `indicators` narrows it and, unlike on /v1/districts, is uncapped — the default is already everything.

| Parameter | Type | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `indicators` | csv | Optional. Omit for the full profile. |
